taskPackages.summary: E-2 safety preflight producer for AlembicAgent. Implement only the AlembicAgent live terminal.exec hardening from Design §10: add src/tools/runtime/handlers/terminalSafety.ts by copying only input-agnostic DENIED_BINS/detectDangerousShellPayload primitives into a live-side wrapper (do not import dead terminal stack); replace terminal.ts local substring deny constants with terminalSafety; fix cwd jail with path.relative boundary; extend ToolContext/registry types with optional auditSink duck type; record exactly one audit attempt for live terminal.exec success/failure with action terminal.exec, result, duration, sha256 commandHash only (do not store command text; audit failure must not change tool result); surface sandboxed=false/degradeReason/fallbackUsed diagnostics in terminal result metadata/output. Do not give Agent write terminal access, do not add Evolution terminal yet, do not delete dead stack yet, do not change AnalyzeGroundingGuard default. Validate with Node >=22: build/typecheck, targeted terminal safety tests covering sudo spacing/quoted bypass, shell payload, rm -fr/fork bomb denial, benign read-only command pass, cwd sibling rejection, audit hash/no raw command, audit sink throwing non-fatal, and sandbox fallback diagnostic. Commit on AlembicAgent main and return TargetResultEnvelope with commit hash, changed files, commands, outputs, residual risks.

E-2 AlembicAgent rework after controller review. Keep commit b2088045's accepted safety/cwd/sandbox work, but fix the audit contract drift only: Design §10 E2-4 requires ToolContext auditSink to be a host-agnostic duck type mirroring AuditLogger.log(entry), and E2-5 requires action terminal.exec, result, duration, data.commandHash=sha256(command) with no raw command text. Current Agent commit defines ToolAuditSinkLike.record(event), terminal.ts calls sink.record(event), and tests only cover record(), so Alembic ToolContextFactory cannot pass tryGet('auditLogger') directly. Rework: replace the record() surface with log(entry); shape ToolAuditEntry to be directly compatible with Alembic AuditLogger.log, including action:'terminal.exec', result, duration, data:{commandHash}, and safe host-agnostic actor/resource/context defaults as needed; keep audit failures non-fatal; ensure every live terminal.exec path attempts exactly one audit when sink exists; remove/replace tests that only prove record(); add targeted tests proving a log sink receives one hash-only entry and a throwing log sink is non-fatal; assert raw command text is absent. Do not support/keep the rejected record() alias unless a source requirement is found; do not expand into E-1 terminal allowlist, E-3 dead-stack deletion, E-4 phantom cleanup, or AnalyzeGroundingGuard. Validate with Node >=22: targeted runtime terminal safety tests, build:check, and any affected contract/public-signature tests. Commit on AlembicAgent main and return TargetResultEnvelope with commit hash, changed files, command outputs, and residual risks.

E-2 AlembicAgent rework-2 after controller raw-evidence review. Rework-1 fixed .log(entry) and data.commandHash, but it still violates the E-2 audit persistence requirement because terminal.ts builds requestId as terminal.exec:<commandHash-prefix>. Alembic AuditLogger.log maps requestId to audit_logs.id, and audit_logs.id is TEXT PRIMARY KEY, so repeated identical commands reuse the same audit id; later inserts fail and are swallowed, meaning not every live terminal.exec leaves an audit row. Scope is ONLY this persistence blocker. Fix by making ToolAuditEntry.requestId optional and omitting it for terminal.exec so AuditLogger generates unique ids, OR by generating a per-invocation unique requestId that is not derived solely from command hash. Preserve action:'terminal.exec', result, duration, data:{commandHash}, no raw command text, .log(entry), and audit failure non-fatal behavior. Add a regression that runs/logs repeated identical commands and proves requestId is absent or unique per entry and the two audit attempts cannot collapse to the same persistence id; keep the hash-only/no-raw-command assertion. Do not expand into E-1 allowlist, E-3 dead-stack deletion/public subpath retirement, E-4 phantom cleanup, E-5 prompt/guard, or Alembic main wiring. Validate with Node >=22: targeted runtime terminal safety tests, build:check, and affected contract/public-signature tests as needed. Commit on AlembicAgent main and return TargetResultEnvelope with commit hash, changed files, command outputs, and residual risks.

E-2 AlembicAgent rework-3 after controller raw-evidence review. Rework-2 correctly fixed terminal.exec audit persistence by omitting/uniquing requestId, but controller source review found a separate E2-7 blocker: execInSandboxOrDirect still overwrites any sandboxExecutor-provided diagnostics with {sandboxed:true,fallbackUsed:false} after executor.exec returns. That makes the later Alembic ToolContextFactory bridge repair impossible to observe from Agent results, violating E2-7 sandbox degradation explicitness. Scope is ONLY this producer contract gap. Preserve all accepted E-2 behavior from prior rounds: structured terminalSafety allowlist/cwd jail, auditSink.log(entry), action terminal.exec, result/duration, data.commandHash only, no raw command text, audit failures non-fatal, and no stable commandHash-derived requestId. Change Agent terminal runtime so SandboxExecutorLike may return optional diagnostics {sandboxed:boolean,fallbackUsed:boolean,degradeReason?:string}; when present, preserve it instead of overwriting. When absent, keep the sandboxed:true/fallbackUsed:false default. Ensure the existing result decoration continues to set _meta.fallbackUsed and output [unsandboxed:<reason>] for fallback/degraded runs. Add a regression where a fake sandboxExecutor returns stdout/stderr/exitCode plus diagnostics {sandboxed:false,fallbackUsed:true,degradeReason:'seatbelt_unavailable'} and assert the terminal.exec ToolResult exposes fallbackUsed plus the unsandboxed diagnostic; this must prove an Alembic bridge can pass degradation through. Keep the existing missing-sandboxExecutor fallback and repeated-audit tests. Do not expand into E-1 allowlist consumer, E-3 dead-stack deletion/public subpath retirement, E-4 phantom cleanup, E-5 prompt/guard, or Alembic main wiring. Validate with Node >=22: targeted runtime terminal safety tests, build:check, tool-v2 contract/public-signature checks as affected, and grep showing no terminal.exec:<hash> requestId and no diagnostics overwrite. Commit on AlembicAgent main and return TargetResultEnvelope with commit hash, changed files, command outputs, and residual risks.

E-2 Alembic main consumer package after accepted AlembicAgent producer commit 1b8d5009da34613272ce93112589897515649d74. Scope is ONLY ToolContextFactory consumer wiring for live terminal.exec safety: (1) E2-6 inject auditSink from the existing single DI factory so daemon/HTTP/CLI tool calls all receive the same audit logger path; (2) E2-7 preserve sandboxExec diagnostics through SandboxExecutorBridge so Agent terminal.exec can expose sandbox fallback/degradation. Current evidence: Alembic/lib/tools/v2/ToolContextFactory.ts create() already builds ToolContext for V2 tools but lacks auditSink, and SandboxExecutorBridge.exec() returns only stdout/stderr/exitCode, dropping sandboxExec result.sandboxed/result.degradeReason. Implement narrowly in Alembic: add auditSink: tryGet(c,'auditLogger') in ToolContextFactory.create(); extend SandboxExecutorBridge return shape to include diagnostics compatible with AlembicAgent's accepted contract {sandboxed:boolean,fallbackUsed:boolean,degradeReason?:string}; map sandboxExec result.sandboxed=false to fallbackUsed:true and carry degradeReason, and sandboxed=true to fallbackUsed:false. Do not change command policy, sandbox profile, filesystem/network intent, command execution semantics, Agent repository, Core, Plugin, E-1 Evolution terminal access, E-3 dead stack deletion/public subpath, E-4 phantom cleanup, or E-5 prompts. Add/adjust tests around ToolContextFactory/V2 tool system proving auditSink comes from container auditLogger and SandboxExecutorBridge/terminal.exec output can surface degraded diagnostics when sandboxExec reports sandboxed:false. If direct bridge unit seams are hard because of dynamic imports, add the smallest testable seam without broad refactor; avoid mock-only success with no real consumer. Validate with Node >=22: npm run build:check, relevant unit tests, lint:repo-boundary, and if touched shared assets then check:shared-asset-drift. Commit on Alembic main and return TargetResultEnvelope with commit hash, changed files, validation outputs, and residual risks.
